thread:
Jonah: quick proposal — redistributed burst lanes for mixed-capacity pools. idea: keep a small per-region on‑demand reserve (15% GPU count) to satisfy egress/locality and latency-sensitive traffic, then allow a global spot/ephemeral lease layer that can borrow capacity across regions when network affinity is low. eviction credits per-tenant to avoid repeated preempt+reschedule churn.

Sophia: sounds promising. how do we handle egress-costs and data-locality constraints? some customers must stay in-region for compliance.

Jonah: agree. plan is that each region enforces a hard tag-based affinity: tagged workloads never cross-region. untagged/latency-tolerant tasks are eligible for cross-region bursting. egress/cost signals feed into lease selection.

Mike: two operational concerns: 1) long init times for some models (cold-start 90s) make short-lived spot bursts wasteful, 2) spot interruption rate spikes during market events. can we gate bursting by task expected runtime and a preemption-tolerance score?

Lina: +1. propose a warm-warm pool: small warm spot set (preloaded model cache) that acts as a short-term buffer with higher min-availability. then deeper spot lanes for batch jobs. also use a runtime heuristic: only burst for expected runtime > 3m or if cache hit probability > 0.6.

Ara: what about metrics and telemetry for this? need SLOs for latency tail, eviction rate, and reschedule amplification. we should also surface per-tenant "eviction credit" balance in console.

Jonah: telemetry plan: add three new histograms and two gauges: burst_latency_tail_p95, eviction_rate_per_min, reschedule_amplification, and gauge eviction_credits_{tenant}. rollouts behind a feature flag.

Lina: pseudoconfig for the pool (very rough):
```yaml
pool: redispatched-global-burst
per_region_min_on_demand: 0.15  # fraction of GPUs
burst_lease_ttl: 600           # seconds
warm_spot_min: 0.05            # fraction kept warm per region
max_cross_region_ratio: 0.3    # fraction of region capacity that can be borrowed
eviction_credit_rate: 1       # credits/sec accrual per active instance
```

Mike: nice. also add a decay window for credits so we don't accumulate forever (e.g., 7d decay). and add a rapid-drain mitigation: if interruption_rate > 0.2 for 5m, reduce cross_region_ratio by 50%.

infra-bot: autoscaler-sim v2 finished: 10k-sim runs, median cost reduction 18%, 95th percentile latency increased 2.8% when cross-region-bursting enabled. full results: https://internal/redwood/sim/2125012345

Sophia: could we file a quick cost model for egress tradeoffs? curious threshold where cross-region bursting flips from win -> loss.

Jonah: yes — Lina can run a sweep. next steps: Lina to prototype scheduler changes + sim, Mike to add preemption-score heuristic, Ara to wire telemetry + console fields. propose canary in eu-west-1 with a single tenant and 10% traffic after tests.

Mike: if we can turn up a canary next week I'm in. will also run chaos preempt tests to validate eviction-crediting behavior.

Jonah: cool. I'll create the spike PR and a tracking ticket. thanks all :rocket:
